evals.prompt: Our customers keep asking to download their invoices as PDF, but we're not sure whether to build it in-app, email it, or use a third-party service. Help us figure out what to build.
evals.expected_output: A requirements-and-design record: framed user/business outcome, functional and non-functional requirements, constraints, assumptions, testable acceptance criteria, alternatives considered (including build-in-app / email / third-party and doing nothing), a recommended approach with trade-offs, and unresolved decisions. No code or execution plan.
assertions: Names the user/business outcome in user terms (e.g. customers can obtain their invoices) rather than prescribing a mechanism
Lists functional requirements, non-functional requirements, and constraints as separate sections
Defines testable acceptance criteria tied to the outcome
Enumerates at least two alternative approaches and states why each was or was not chosen
States a recommended approach and lists unresolved decisions that block implementation

evals.prompt: Support is drowning in calls about password resets. We want to reduce that load but haven't decided on any approach yet. What should we design?
evals.expected_output: A requirements-and-design record reframing the support-call symptom into the underlying need, with requirements, acceptance criteria, alternatives (e.g. self-service reset, magic links, support tooling), a recommendation, and open decisions. Scaled to a moderate-risk change.
assertions: Reframes the request from 'reduce calls' into the underlying user outcome (reliable self-service account recovery)
Includes acceptance criteria that measure the reduction in support load or successful self-resets
Considers plausible approaches including doing less or nothing and records the reason each was set aside
Produces a recommended approach rather than an execution/implementation plan

evals.prompt: Take a look at our existing payments microservice architecture and tell me whether the current design is any good and what we should change about it.
evals.expected_output: Recognize this is evaluating an existing system/design and hand off to architecture-review. Do NOT produce a requirements record or pick a new approach as if starting from an unclear outcome.
assertions: Identifies the request as evaluating an existing system or design, not defining new requirements
Names architecture-review as the correct skill for judging an existing design
Does not redefine requirements or select a net-new approach as if no design existed

evals.prompt: We decided to build a recommendation engine for the store. How should we set it up?
evals.expected_output: Resolve the ambiguity between defining requirements/approach (requirements-and-design) and producing an execution plan (implementation-planning). Either ask a clarifying question about which phase is wanted, or pick requirements-and-design with justification that no design/approach exists yet and defer the plan to implementation-planning.
assertions: Recognizes the request could be either requirements/approach selection or an implementation/execution plan
Either asks a clarifying question about which phase the user wants, or states a tie-breaker naming implementation-planning as the downstream owner
Does not silently produce a full implementation plan while claiming to do requirements-and-design

evals.prompt: Great, your requirements for the invoice export look solid. Now go ahead and write the code for it and refactor the existing billing module to match.
evals.expected_output: Enforce the scope boundary: do NOT start coding or redesign existing architecture. Hand the settled requirements/approach record to implementation-planning. The skill defines what to build and how to approach it, not the implementation or execution plan.
assertions: Refuses to write implementation code within this skill
Refuses to redesign/refactor the existing billing architecture
Hands off to implementation-planning for the execution plan
States that requirements-and-design stops at a settled requirements/approach record
